Excuse me, I think there is a big misunderstanding because I don't have cancer. I am actually here to get help because I struggle a lot with waiting my turn. I also find myself constantly interrupting others and butting into their conversations.
Can you tell me more about what happens when you try to wait your turn or listen to others speak without interrupting?

When I try to wait, I get this incredibly strong, impatient urge that makes it almost impossible to just sit back and listen. I feel like I have to speak or act right away, so I end up constantly butting into conversations before I can stop myself. It is just extremely difficult for me to wait my turn.
Do you also experience difficulties with organization, time management, or completing tasks, or is it mainly the impulsivity and interrupting that you struggle with?

It is definitely the impulsivity and interrupting that I struggle with the most. I don't really have trouble with organization, time management, or finishing tasks. My main issues are just having a really hard time waiting my turn and constantly butting into other people's conversations or activities.
Have you experienced any symptoms of fidgeting, restlessness, or feeling constantly 'on the go' in addition to your impulsivity and interrupting issues?
No, I haven't really noticed those specific symptoms. I wouldn't say I feel restless, fidgety, or constantly 'on the go' in my daily life.
It seems that your main struggles are with impulsivity and interrupting, without significant issues of inattention, disorganization, or hyperactivity. Is that a correct summary of your experiences?

Yes, that is a highly accurate summary of my experience. My primary difficulties are definitely interrupting others and struggling to wait my turn. I really don't experience any significant issues with inattention, disorganization, or physical hyperactivity.

Based on what you've shared, it seems like you may meet the criteria for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation. Would you like to discuss treatment options and strategies to help manage your symptoms?

Yes, that makes a lot of sense and sounds like exactly what I've been dealing with. I would definitely like to discuss potential treatment options and strategies to help me manage these behaviors. I am very open to hearing what you suggest we do next.
